title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 5
paragraphs: This, then, is the Persian account, and they trace the beginning of their quarrel with the Hellenes to the capture of Ilion. As for Io, the Phoenicians do not tell the story the way the Persians do. They deny that they carried her off to Egypt by force, and say instead that while she was at Argos she became intimate with the captain of their ship, and when she discovered that she was pregnant and was too ashamed to confess it to her parents, she sailed off with the Phoenicians of her own accord, for fear of being found out. So much for the tales told by the Persians and Phoenicians respectively. As for myself, I am not going to say whether things happened this way or that — but once I have pointed out the man who, within my own knowledge, first began to do wrong to the Hellenes, I shall move forward with my account, describing the cities of men, small as well as great. For those that were once great have for the most part become small, while those that are great in my own time were small in earlier days. Knowing that human prosperity never stays long in the same place, I shall treat both alike.
